name: Sapphire FUE

card.summary: FUE variant using sapphire-tipped blades for recipient incisions; promoted as finer, with little independent evidence yet.
card.note: Advantages are largely claimed by clinics; one 2026 comparison study exists.

quick.overview:
Sapphire FUE is a variant of hair transplantation in which recipient channels are cut with sapphire blades rather than steel ones.

Clinics describe finer incisions that may allow denser placement and faster healing; evidence comparing the two blade types is limited.
quick.mechanism: Follicles are extracted as in standard FUE, then implanted into channels made with sapphire-tipped blades, which Grokipedia describes as sharper with incisions of about 0.5 to 1.0 mm.
quick.risks: Risks are those of FUE in general, such as swelling, shock loss and folliculitis. A registered trial examined a topical agent for wound healing after sapphire FUE.

lead: Sapphire FUE is a follicular unit extraction hair transplant in which the recipient sites, the small openings where grafts are placed, are made with sapphire blades instead of steel.[1] It is used to restore hair density and a natural-looking hairline for people with pattern baldness, with clinics promoting finer incisions that allow denser placement and quicker healing.[1][3]

In FUE generally, individual follicular units of one to four hairs are removed under local anaesthesia and the surgeon makes small recipient openings, set in a deliberate density and angle so the result looks natural; FUE leaves small dot-like scars rather than the linear scar of strip harvesting.[3] Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, says sapphire blades are sharper and finer, with possible advantages in bleeding, healing and scar visibility; these are descriptions rather than independently verified findings.[1]
A 2026 prospective observational study of 1000 patients compared sapphire and steel blades and reported higher graft survival with sapphire.[2]

paras: FUE removes individual follicular units with tiny circular punches about 0.6 to 1.0 mm wide and places them in recipient sites made with micro blades or needles.[3] Sapphire FUE changes the blade material of that recipient step.[1] Wikipedia's hair transplantation article does not address blade material; it records common cosmetic goals including male pattern baldness, hairline lowering or reconstruction, eyebrow restoration and scar filling.[3]

Grokipedia describes sapphire blades as allowing denser placement, less bleeding, faster healing and less visible scarring, and gives channel sizes of 0.5 to 1.0 mm.[1] Wikipedia lists shock loss of transplanted hair, a steep learning curve, higher cost and longer surgery time as general characteristics of FUE.[3]

A 2026 prospective observational study in the Journal of Maxillofacial and Oral Surgery followed 1000 hair-restoration patients from January 2024 to March 2025. The sapphire group had higher graft survival (94.7%) than the steel group (88.9%), double-forceps implantation shortened implantation time by 1.3 hours, two-day full-head operations gave higher density (43.2 grafts per cm2) and satisfaction, and half-head sessions healed in 4.6 days versus 6.1.[2] A completed registered trial of 70 participants studied topical rifamycin SV for wound healing after sapphire FUE.[4] The 2026 study was observational rather than randomized.

timeline.event: Registered trial of topical rifamycin SV after sapphire FUE begins.[4]
Observational comparison of sapphire and steel FUE blades published.[2]

angle.text: Sapphire FUE is chosen as a way to rebuild a hairline and add density with fine incisions. Clinics say the finer blades let grafts sit closely and heal quickly.
